hooks.text: An explosion shone twenty times brighter than our entire Milky Way galaxy.
One cosmic flash reached a peak brightness 570 billion times the Sun.
Telescopes in Chile spotted a cosmic explosion that defied the laws of physics.

title: The Explosion That Outshone the Galaxy
description: ASASSN-15lh reached a brightness 570 billion times greater than the Sun, creating a cosmic mystery that challenges our understanding of physics.

beats.text: An explosion shone twenty times brighter than our entire Milky Way galaxy.
beats.visual: Artist's concept of a superluminous supernova explosion, 2015

beats.text: In June 2015, twin automated telescopes in Chile discovered a dot of light named ASASSN-15lh.
beats.visual: Cerro Tololo Inter-American Observatory telescope dome, Chile, 2015
subjects: All Sky Automated Survey for SuperNovae

beats.text: This monster reached a peak brightness 570 billion times greater than our Sun.
beats.visual: Artist concept comparing a supernova's brilliance to a nearby sun, 2015

beats.text: It crossed 3.8 billion light-years with a strange spectrum that completely lacked hydrogen and helium.
beats.visual: South African Large Telescope dome under the night sky, 2015

beats.text: Unlike common supernovae found in small galaxies, this blast erupted inside a massive, quiet galaxy.
beats.visual: Hubble Space Telescope image of a massive distant galaxy, 2016

beats.text: The event radiated more total energy than our Sun will emit in its entire lifetime.
beats.visual: Close-up of the Sun's surface showing solar flares and energy, 2015
queries: Sun solar flare extreme close up

beats.text: Astronomers debate if it was a fast-spinning magnetar or a Kerr black hole shredding a star.
beats.visual: Artist's concept of a black hole tearing a star apart, 2016
queries: black hole shredding star artist concept

beats.text: That ongoing debate still leaves astronomers trying to explain why an explosion shone twenty times brighter than our entire Milky Way galaxy.
beats.visual: Wide panorama of the Milky Way galaxy seen from Earth
